roles.heroLead: Beautiful tile gets the compliments; the membrane behind it earns them. roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Kirkland, WA?
roles.costP1: Kirkland tile projects price at roughly $14–$26 per square foot installed — tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor together, with the labor share starting at $11/sq ft. A tub-shower surround of standard size comes to $3,200–$6,800; take the bathroom all the way — floor, shower, niche — and most totals fall between $6,500 and $14,000.
roles.costP2: A design truth that doubles as a budgeting truth: the format sets the labor, not the price per box. Handmade-look zellige and small mosaics eat hours in cuts and grout lines, which is how a $4 sheet can out-cost a $12 large-format porcelain plank at install time.
roles.costNote: Ranges for Kirkland homes and condos, August 2026 — installed, with tile, materials and labor counted. The written quote from the free estimate is the real figure.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers, and the order isn't negotiable. When a shower fails somewhere around Kirkland and we're called to open it, a layer is missing — the membrane, almost always — a few hundred dollars trimmed once, five figures paid to undo it.
roles.whyP1: No leak introduces itself. Water moves past grout, sits in the substrate, and turns up two years later as a hallway floor with give or a stain blooming on the ceiling of the room below. By that stage the scope reads framing, subfloor, drywall — and the tile you loved, done twice.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing runs about 10% of a shower's budget. Cutting it is the priciest decision available in a bathroom remodel — and the least visible one.
roles.scopeIntro: Starting prices, honestly labeled — format, substrate condition and layout ambition all move them. The firm number is written at your place, free.
roles.cardShower: Waterproofed from the studs out: pre-sloped base, bonded membrane, documented flood test, then the niche, the curb or curbless entry, then tile. The unglamorous half of the job is the valuable half.
roles.cardFloors: Bathrooms, kitchens, entries, mudrooms, condo baths and basements. We flatten the subfloor and specify an uncoupling membrane where movement or radiant heat calls for one.
roles.cardBacksplash: Zellige, subway, herringbone, mosaic sheet or slab-look porcelain — outlet cuts kept crisp, edges trimmed properly, grout chosen against your counter, not the tile carton.
roles.cardHeated: Radiant electric mat over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-tested before setting and after grout, on its own circuit. An upgrade that only makes sense while the floor is open.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked field tile, tired grout, shower corners pulling loose. We'll say plainly whether a repair is honest or the substrate behind it has already failed.
roles.cardDemo: Old tile, thinset and backer removed under sheeting and negative air, hauled the same day. HOA elevator rules and parking limits handled without drama.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Kirkland, WA?
roles.faqA1: In Kirkland, tile installation comes to about $14 to $26 per square foot installed once tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor are added up — labor on its own starts near $11 per square foot. Standard tub-shower surrounds run $3,200 to $6,800; a bathroom carried through completely, floor and shower and niche, usually totals $6,500 to $14,000. Note that format outweighs unit price: mosaic sheets and large-format planks both require substantially more labor per square foot than standard 12×12 tile.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Kirkland?
roles.faqA2: Tiled showers in Kirkland cost $3,200 to $6,800 for the standard alcove — demolition, bonded waterproofing, a pre-sloped base or pan, setting, niche and grout all included. Designer scope moves the number up: curbless entries, benches, steam enclosures, full-height stone or zellige walls. Waterproofing is only about a tenth of the total, and it's the tenth that prevents the tens-of-thousands failure.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes — no exceptions, no matter how ambitious the tile. Every shower gets a bonded waterproofing system: pre-sloped base, sheet or liquid membrane up the walls, corners, seams and penetrations sealed, and a 24-hour flood test that we document before setting begins. Cement board with thinset over it is not waterproofing. Water passes tile and grout freely; only the membrane keeps it away from framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: A Kirkland bathroom runs four to six working days: demolition and dust protection first, then substrate plus waterproofing with its 24-hour flood test, then a day or two of tile setting, and finally grout, silicone and trim. Add 24 more hours for grout cure before the first shower. A floor alone is typically a one-or-two-day project, condos included.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Different jobs. Porcelain — denser, sub-0.5% water absorption, harder to chip — is the call for floors, showers and any wet or high-traffic surface. Ceramic costs less and looks every bit as good on walls and backsplashes. Our Kirkland rule: porcelain underfoot and in shower floors, always; ceramic, glass or zellige where the surface's whole job is beauty.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes. An electric radiant mat beneath the tile costs $11 to $16 per square foot installed, thermostat in the price, and since the work only pencils while the floor is already open, it's the best-value indulgence in the remodel. The mat goes over an uncoupling membrane, is resistance-tested twice — before and after setting — and gets a dedicated circuit of its own.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Almost always yes. Demolition with haul-away is around $3.50 per square foot, and it's the only way to actually see the subfloor — rot, movement, past moisture — and to land the new floor at the right height against doorways and cabinetry. Over-tiling an existing floor works only when it's flat, sound and well bonded, and even then it hides conditions better discovered during demo than after the grout has cured.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Kirkland?
roles.faqA8: For a typical 30-square-foot run, a Kirkland kitchen backsplash installs at $1,100 to $2,200, with outlet cuts, edge trim and grout matched to the counter included. The designer end of the range — zellige, mosaic sheets, herringbone, a framed feature behind the range, slab-look porcelain to the ceiling — costs more because layout and cutting time rise, not because the tile necessarily does.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often. Repair and regrout pricing starts at $8 per square foot, and it's the right scope for stained or crumbling grout, a couple of impact-cracked tiles, or shower corners due for silicone in place of grout. It's the wrong scope when the substrate has gone: hollow-sounding tile, tiles loosening in a pattern, or soft spots in the wall mean a patch buys months only. We inspect first and tell you which yours is before any quote.
roles.faqQ10: Which Kirkland neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Kirkland — Moss Bay, Market, Norkirk, Highlands, Everest, Lakeview, Central Houghton, Carillon Point, Bridle Trails, North and South Rose Hill, Kingsgate, Totem Lake, North and South Juanita and Finn Hill — condos downtown included, plus Bellevue, Redmond, Bothell, Kenmore, Woodinville and the rest of the Eastside and Seattle.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Every OC Flooring tile installation carries a 2-year workmanship warranty — twice the term we give carpet, because tile defects reveal themselves in year two rather than week two. When the shower uses a manufacturer's full waterproofing assembly, their system warranty adds to ours. Membrane and flood test are photographed on every job, so the record is there for a future appraisal or sale.
